newsitem.title: CANADA: Duracell to close Mississauga manufacturing plant.
newsitem.headline: Duracell to close Mississauga manufacturing plant.

text.p: Duracell said Tuesday it will phase out manufacturing operations at its Mississauga, Ont., facility over a six-month period beginning in July, resulting in the loss of 110 manufacturing, technical and support jobs.

The facility produces AA-size Duracell alkaline batteries. Duracell said it will maintain sales, marketing, distribution and administrative functions at its Mississauga, Montreal, Calgary, Alberta, and Vancouver, British Columbia, operations to serve the Canadian market.
The decision follows a comprehensive review of Duracell's global manufacturing infrastructure, it said.

"The company is consolidating production to more effectively use plant capacity, better manage capital assets, and ensure the ability to more efficiently service other major markets," said Joe Dooley, President, Duracell Canada Inc.
Duracell, a unit of Gillette Co., said it will provide the affected employees severance payments, benefits and help in finding new jobs.
Gillette's stock fell 87.5 cents to $88.75 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
